title: console: single-membership users get no current-organization indicator on multi-org (isolated) deployments — workspace-switcher only renders for multi-membership users
body:
## Summary

On a multi-org deployment (`tenancy posture: isolated`, enterprise `@objectstack/organizations` mounted), a business user who is a member of **exactly one** organization gets **no indication anywhere in the console of which organization they are in**: the top bar shows no current-organization name, and the `workspace-switcher` control does not render at all for them. Only users with multiple memberships (e.g. an admin joined to two orgs) get the switcher — which doubles as the only place the current org name is displayed.

With row-level isolation active, "which organization am I looking at" is load-bearing context (all lists are silently scoped). A single-membership user has no way to tell.

## Repro

1. Boot a host app with `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED=true` and a licensed `@objectstack/organizations` (posture `isolated`, not degraded); two organizations exist.
2. Create user A as a member of org 1 only (membership policy `invite-only`, default active org = org 1). Create admin as member of both orgs.
3. Log in as admin: top bar renders the workspace switcher with both orgs, current org name visible. ✔
4. Log in as user A: no org name anywhere on the page (checked full-page text), and the workspace-switcher element is absent — probed at 3s/8s/15s/22s after load to rule out delayed hydration.

Observed on `@objectstack/*@17.0.0` (console served by the host app), Chrome.

## Ask

Render a read-only "current organization" indicator for single-membership users (switcher itself can stay hidden when there is nothing to switch to). App projects have no metadata hook to provide this themselves — the top bar is console-owned.

Found during a downstream project's multi-tenant acceptance run (steedos-labs/os-project-titanwind-ehr #1577, case S20-001; screenshots archived there).
